hero.title: 🗝️ Dungeon Name Generator
hero.tagline: Crypts, caves, wizard's towers and drowned temples, from the Sunken Crypt of Vael to Oswin's Folly.

article.intro: Good dungeon names tell the players what they're walking into before they light the first torch: a crypt, a mine, a wizard's tower gone wrong. This **dungeon name generator** makes names for D&D and other fantasy games in eight kinds, from crypts and goblin caves to wizard's lairs and shifting mazes, and can add a one-line hook to get the adventure started.

sections.heading: Eight good dungeon names
sections.content:
All eight came from the generator:

  • The Mouldering Ossuary of the Silent Order: a crypt with a backstory in the name.
  • The Webbed Hollows: a cave that warns the players about spiders.
  • The Siege-Scarred Castle: a ruined fortress whose name tells you what happened.
  • Oswin's Folly: a wizard's lair where "a failed experiment has fused two rooms and their occupants".
  • The Drowned Fane of the Spider Mother: a fane is an old word for a temple.
  • The Singing Iron Workings: a mine with something strange in it.
  • The Old Greymarket Storm Drains: an under-the-city dungeon named like a real place.
  • The Maze That Breathes: a labyrinth with a name that makes players nervous.

sections.heading: What makes a dungeon name work
sections.content:
The word itself has moved. Dungeon comes from the Old French donjon, the great tower or keep of a castle, and only later came to mean the cells underneath. Since D&D was published in 1974, it has meant any place full of monsters and treasure, from a tomb to a sewer.

  • Say what it is. Catacombs, Ossuary, Warrens, Workings, Cisterns: the kind of place tells players what to expect.
  • Add one detail. Moss-Grown, Bone-Strewn, Smoke-Stained: an adjective is a description the players hear before they arrive.
  • Name it after someone for a lair or a tomb: Morwenna's Puzzle-House, The Pale Crypt of Nerith.

The eight kinds use real words for each place: an ossuary holds bones, an undercroft is the vaulted cellar under a church, an adit is the level entrance to a mine, and firedamp was the miners' name for explosive gas. Choose With a DM hook for a one-line reason to go in, like The Pit of Orvane: The local troll is reasonable, but only if you bring cheese.

sections.heading: Running your dungeon
sections.content:
• Use the hook as the rumour the players hear in the tavern, then decide whether it's true.
  • Name the rooms too. A dungeon with a Bell Room and a Drowned Stair is easier to map and remember.
  • Link it to the world above. A mine belongs to a town; a crypt belongs to a family; a ruin belonged to someone's castle.

For the castle the ruin used to be, try the Castle Name Generator. For whoever gives the players the job, the NPC Name Generator makes a name, a job and a quirk. For every race and class, see all the D&D name generators.

For more, see all the world-building name generators.

faqs.question: What are good D&D dungeon names?
faqs.answer: Names that say what kind of place it is and add one detail, like The Webbed Hollows, The Singing Iron Workings or The Mouldering Ossuary of the Silent Order. Add a DM hook for a reason to go in.

faqs.question: What does dungeon originally mean?
faqs.answer: It comes from the Old French donjon, the keep or great tower of a castle. The meaning of a prison underneath came later.

faqs.question: Can I use these in a published adventure?
faqs.answer: Yes, they're free to use. Search a name first if you're publishing, in case another adventure already uses it.
